title: Indian Capital Gains Tax on Stocks and Mutual Funds (Union Budget 2024)
content:
Taxation on capital appreciation from equity investments in India is governed by the Income Tax Act under two primary heads: Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) and Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG). The Union Budget 2024, announced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in July 2024, introduced substantial structural changes to capital gains tax rates.

1. Equity Shares and Equity-Oriented Mutual Funds:
- Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG under Section 111A): If listed equity shares or equity mutual fund units are sold within 12 months (1 year) of purchase, the profit is classified as short-term capital gains. Effective July 23, 2024, STCG on equity is taxed at a flat rate of 20% (increased from the previous rate of 15%), plus applicable surcharge and 4% health and education cess.
- Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG under Section 112A): If equity holdings are maintained for more than 12 months before sale, the profit qualifies as long-term capital gains. Effective July 23, 2024, LTCG is taxed at a flat rate of 12.5% (increased from 10%). However, the annual tax-free exemption threshold was raised from ₹1,00,000 to ₹1,25,000 per financial year. Only aggregate long-term equity capital gains exceeding ₹1.25 Lakhs are subject to the 12.5% tax.

2. Unlisted Shares and Other Financial Assets:
For unlisted shares, the holding period for qualifying as LTCG is 24 months, with taxation set at 12.5% without indexation benefit.

3. Setting Off Capital Losses:
Short-term capital losses can be set off against both short-term and long-term capital gains. Long-term capital losses can only be set off against long-term capital gains. Unadjusted capital losses can be carried forward for up to 8 assessment years, provided the income tax return (ITR) is filed before the prescribed due date.
